changes: Add fair treatment of staff and suppliers as an explicit ethical consideration, since the card covers staff only in passing and does not mention suppliers.
Frame the social and environmental effects point around decision-making, as the Units 3 and 4 study design expects, rather than as a general awareness point.
match.reason: The bank card covers the same ethical ideas at a similar level, but it lacks the explicit supplier and staff fairness point and is pitched at Units 1 and 2, so it needs small changes for Units 3 and 4.

confirm.reason: The bank point is a Units 1 and 2 introduction centred on honest recording and privacy, while this Year 12 point is about weighing ethics in business decisions, including fair treatment of staff and suppliers, which the card does not cover; matching it would mean changing its content and depth.

draft.title: Ethical considerations
card: Ethics is about what is right and fair, not only what the law allows. Business owners and accountants make decisions that affect many people.
reports should show the true position and performance of the business. They should not hide debts or overstate profit to mislead owners, lenders or the tax office.
staff should be paid what they are owed and work in safe conditions. Suppliers should be paid on the agreed terms and not misled about when payment will come.
a business can affect the environment through waste or pollution, and the community through jobs and local impact. A good decision weighs these effects as well as profit.
draft.remember: Ethical decisions weigh honesty, fair treatment of staff and suppliers, and effects on the environment and community, not just profit.

a.q: Which action shows honesty in reporting?
opts: Recording a large unpaid loan as a liability
Delaying a loan record until after the year ends
Leaving out a debt when the owner is selling
Listing sales that have not yet happened as income
a.why: Recording the loan shows the true position of the business, so users of the report are not misled. The other options hide a debt or inflate results, which gives readers a false picture.
a.clue: Which action gives readers the true picture?

b.q: Priya owns a bakery in Geelong. Cash is tight, so she pays her flour supplier 60 days late with no warning, though the agreed terms are 30 days. Which ethical consideration does this mainly break?
b.why: The supplier is not being paid on the agreed terms and was not told, so this is unfair treatment of a supplier. Honesty in reporting is the tempting choice, but nothing here says the reports were changed or misstated.
b.clue: Who is affected by the late payment?

a.best: Recording a large unpaid loan as a liability
